Looking at this problem, I need to determine whether the standard inclusion SO(3) ↪ SO⁺(3,1) (fixing a timelike vector) lifts to an injective homomorphism Spin(3) → Spin(3,1) commuting with the double covers.

Let me work through this carefully.

## Proof

**Setup and notation.** Let $V$ be a 4-dimensional real vector space with inner product of signature $(3,1)$, and let $e_0$ be a timelike unit vector. The orthogonal complement $W = e_0^\perp$ is a 3-dimensional positive-definite subspace. The subgroup of $SO^+(3,1)$ (the identity component) fixing $e_0$ is canonically isomorphic to $SO(W) \cong SO(3)$, giving an inclusion
$$i: SO(3) \hookrightarrow SO^+(3,1).$$
Let $\pi_3: \mathrm{Spin}(3) \to SO(3)$ and $\pi_{3,1}: \mathrm{Spin}(3,1) \to SO^+(3,1)$ denote the universal (double) covering maps, with kernels $\ker \pi_3 = \{\pm 1\}$ and $\ker \pi_{3,1} = \{\pm \tilde{e}\}$ respectively.

**Step 1: Existence of the lift.** Consider the composition
$$f := i \circ \pi_3 : \mathrm{Spin}(3) \to SO^+(3,1).$$
The group $\mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong SU(2) \cong S^3$ is simply connected, and $\pi_{3,1}: \mathrm{Spin}(3,1) \to SO^+(3,1)$ is a covering map. By the **lifting lemma for covering spaces**, any continuous map from a simply connected space into the base of a covering lifts to the total space. Thus there exists a unique continuous map
$$\tilde{\imath}: \mathrm{Spin}(3) \to \mathrm{Spin}(3,1)$$
with $\tilde{\imath}(e) = \tilde{e}$ (identity to identity) such that
$$\pi_{3,1} \circ \tilde{\imath} = f = i \circ \pi_3. \tag{$\star$}$$

**Step 2: $\tilde{\imath}$ is a homomorphism.** For any $g \in \mathrm{Spin}(3)$, consider the two maps $\alpha_g, \beta_g : \mathrm{Spin}(3) \to \mathrm{Spin}(3,1)$ defined by
$$\alpha_g(h) = \tilde{\imath}(gh), \qquad \beta_g(h) = \tilde{\imath}(g)\,\tilde{\imath}(h).$$
Both are lifts of the same map $h \mapsto f(gh) = i(\pi_3(gh)) = i(\pi_3(g))\, i(\pi_3(h))$, and
$$\pi_{3,1}(\beta_g(h)) = \pi_{3,1}(\tilde{\imath}(g))\,\pi_{3,1}(\tilde{\imath}(h)) = f(g)\,f(h) = f(gh) = \pi_{3,1}(\alpha_g(h)).$$
At $h = e$: $\alpha_g(e) = \tilde{\imath}(g) = \beta_g(e)$. By uniqueness of lifts (both lifts agree at one point), $\alpha_g = \beta_g$ for all $g$, i.e., $\tilde{\imath}(gh) = \tilde{\imath}(g)\tilde{\imath}(h)$. So $\tilde{\imath}$ is a group homomorphism.

**Step 3: Commutativity.** Equation $(\star)$ is precisely the statement that the diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc} \mathrm{Spin}(3) & \xrightarrow{\tilde{\imath}} & \mathrm{Spin}(3,1) \\ {\scriptstyle \pi_3}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle \pi_{3,1}} \\ SO(3) & \xrightarrow{i} & SO^+(3,1) \end{array}$$
commutes.

**Step 4: Injectivity.** From $(\star)$, if $g \in \ker \tilde{\imath}$, then $i(\pi_3(g)) = \pi_{3,1}(\tilde{\imath}(g)) = \tilde{e}$, so $\pi_3(g) = e$ (since $i$ is injective), giving $g \in \ker \pi_3 = \{\pm 1\}$. Thus
$$\ker \tilde{\imath} \subseteq \{\pm 1\}.$$

It remains to determine whether $-1 \in \ker \tilde{\imath}$. Suppose for contradiction that $\tilde{\imath}(-1) = \tilde{e}$. Then $\tilde{\imath}$ factors through $\mathrm{Spin}(3)/\{\pm 1\} \cong SO(3)$, yielding a homomorphism $j: SO(3) \to \mathrm{Spin}(3,1)$ with $\pi_{3,1} \circ j = i$. This would mean the inclusion $i$ **lifts** to the universal cover $\mathrm{Spin}(3,1)$.

We now show this is impossible. The group $\mathrm{Spin}(3,1) \cong SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ is simply connected (via polar decomposition $A = UP$ with $U \in SU(2) \cong S^3$ and $P = \exp(H)$, $H$ traceless Hermitian, which is contractible; so $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ deformation retracts to $SU(2) \cong S^3$). Hence $\pi_{3,1}$ is the **universal cover**, and a map $i: SO(3) \to SO^+(3,1)$ lifts to $\mathrm{Spin}(3,1)$ if and only if the induced map on fundamental groups satisfies
$$i_*\big(\pi_1(SO(3))\big) \subseteq (\pi_{3,1})_*\big(\pi_1(\mathrm{Spin}(3,1))\big) = 0.$$

Now, $SO^+(3,1)$ deformation retracts onto $SO(3)$: by the polar decomposition in $SO^+(3,1)$, every element decomposes uniquely as a rotation (fixing $e_0$) times a boost (in the $e_0$–spatial direction), and the boost part lies in the contractible space of symmetric positive-definite transformations. Therefore the inclusion $i: SO(3) \hookrightarrow SO^+(3,1)$ is a **homotopy equivalence**, and the induced map
$$i_* : \pi_1(SO(3)) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2 \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; \pi_1(SO^+(3,1)) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$$
is an **isomorphism**. In particular, $i_*$ is not the zero map, so $i$ does **not** lift to the universal cover $\mathrm{Spin}(3,1)$.

This contradicts our assumption that $\tilde{\imath}(-1) = \tilde{e}$. Therefore $\tilde{\imath}(-1) \neq \tilde{e}$, which forces $\tilde{\imath}(-1) = -\tilde{e}$ (the nontrivial element of $\ker \pi_{3,1}$, consistent with $(\star)$: $\pi_{3,1}(-\tilde{e}) = e = i(\pi_3(-1)) = i(e) = e$).

Hence $\ker \tilde{\imath} = \{1\}$, and $\tilde{\imath}$ is **injective**.

**Conclusion.** The inclusion $i: SO(3) \hookrightarrow SO^+(3,1)$ induced by the orthogonal complement of a timelike vector does lift to an injective homomorphism $\tilde{\imath}: \mathrm{Spin}(3) \to \mathrm{Spin}(3,1)$ that commutes with the double covering maps. $\blacksquare$
